acceptance: Changing a file under `.github/workflows/` or `.github/actions/` makes `make pr-preflight` run every test under `tests/unit/workflows`, plus any test file elsewhere that names the changed file (such as `tests/system/test_ci_lint_parity.py` for `ci.yml`).
The existing `oracle-` mapping still selects the oracle scenario tests.
`tests/unit/scripts/test_preflight_targets.py` covers a non-oracle workflow change and a composite-action change selecting those tests.
context:

description:
`_project/scripts/preflight_targets.py` maps a changed non-Python path to tests only through the `SOURCE_GUARD_TESTS` prefixes, and the only workflow prefix there is `.github/workflows/oracle-`. Changing any other workflow selects nothing, although tests read those files: under `tests/unit/workflows` and `tests/system`, 20 test files mention `ci.yml`, 9 `nightly-v2.yml`, 6 `trunk.yml` and 4 `trunk-coverage.yml`. On #3725, a commit that edited `ci.yml` and `nightly-v2.yml` passed preflight with only the 7 tests mapped from the branch's Python changes. The 1,033 workflow and CI-parity tests ran only because they were started by hand, so a broken workflow test would have surfaced one CI round later.

Matching test files by workflow name is not enough on its own: several tests under `tests/unit/workflows` check every workflow in the directory (for example `test_workflow_context_availability.py`, `test_workflow_dispatch_dedupe.py`, `test_ci_text_edit_skip.py`), so a name match would miss them. Composite actions under `.github/actions/` have the same gap. The whole `tests/unit/workflows` directory plus `tests/system/test_ci_lint_parity.py` (1,033 tests) ran serially in about three minutes on #3725.
